newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Foreigners may get to buy Petrobras shares - paper.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners may get to buy Petrobras shares - paper.

text.p: A draft bill to regulate the opening of Brazil's oil sector would allow foreign investors to buy common voting shares of state oil monopoly Petrobras, a local newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil financial daily said the draft rules, which would regulate Brazil's new Petroleum Law, also bar Petrobras from directly distributing natural gas to large consumers.
The paper said the draft bill would maintain a requirement that the federal government own a majority of Petrobras capital stock but would allow it to place 30 percent of the common shares it owns.
The rules, if approved, would replace a law barring foreign ownership of Petrobras capital stock and limiting native Brazilians to just 0.1 percent, it said.
Gazeta quoting Petrobras President Joel Renno as saying the government has not yet decided on a time frame for selling Petrobras common.

It said rumors the government would seek to lift limits against foreign ownership of Petrobras common is responsible for a hike in Petrobras preferred and common share prices on the Sao Paulo bourse in recent sessions.
